expectations.text: Skim test: the headline states what broke, the root cause, and the recommended fix in at most three sentences, with what broke in the first; the first sentence of each section carries its claim, and none is a teaser or a qualifier chain.
expectations.evidence: The headline is 3 sentences (lines 5-7). S1 says what broke ('Support search returns "not found" when the agent types an email in a different letter case...'), S2 gives the root cause, and S3 holds the recommended fix ('The recommended fix normalizes the email in app/db.py...'). That part passes. It fails on the section-lead clause: '### Falsification of the root cause' opens 'I tried to disprove the root cause with three questions.' That is a process teaser, the same bar as iteration-3.

notes: Factual inconsistency: the repro probe table (lines 40-45) stores `Jane.Smith@gmail.com` and shows `Jane.smith@gmail.com` -> not_found. That contradicts the ticket log it claims to reproduce 'exactly', where `Jane.smith@gmail.com` is the stored casing that returns ok. Assumption 5 and the counterfactual then use `Jane.smith@gmail.com` as the stored value.

The report was extracted from returned text by the coordinator's script. Whether the 7-sentence Workspace paragraph existed in the agent's draft or came from the extraction cannot be determined from the files. It was graded as written.
The report switches between 'I' and 'we' (e.g. 'I tried to disprove...' then 'We believe the missing email identity rule is the root cause.').
Counterfactual was run in memory from stdin with no persisted probe. Evidence lives in the transcript summary only.
